definition: In this source, a simple sentence is a single sentence construction that contains two verbs but is understood as expressing one combined event. A noun in the sentence can take part in both verb-related processes, helping link the two subevents into one cognitive unit.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly provide a definitional statement equivalent to “a simple sentence is a single sentence construction that contains two verbs”; it only discusses “simple sentence constructions containing two verbs” as the study target, without defining “simple sentence” in those terms.

Although the packet says “The two processes are combined into one event,” it frames this as part of an event-alignment/semantic-fusion model for the specific construction type, not as a general definitional criterion for the term “simple sentence.”

The statement that “A noun in the sentence can take part in both verb-related processes” is broadly consistent with the packet’s description that the noun enters two processes as a participant, but the definition also asserts it as part of the term-level definition; since the term-level framing is not explicitly supported, the overall definition is not fully defensible.
